metadata.name: Zeabur Builder
metadata.summary: Builds images from your Git repositories and keeps them in the cluster, so services can deploy from Git.

declaration.networkPolicies:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: zot-builder
  namespace: zot
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: zot}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
    - from:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels: {kubernetes.io/metadata.name: builder-system}
          podSelector:
            matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: buildkitd}
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels: {kubernetes.io/metadata.name: builder-system}
          podSelector:
            matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: zeabur-builder}
        # Any Pod in a project namespace can set this label.
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels: {zeabur.com/project: "true"}
          podSelector:
            matchExpressions:
              - {key: builder.zeabur.com/buildrun, operator: Exists}
      ports:
        - {port: 5000, protocol: TCP}

releases.manifests:
# Signs the CA below; nothing else uses it.
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: zot-selfsigned
  namespace: zot
spec:
  selfSigned: {}
---
# A CA of its own: no public CA signs *.svc names. Nodes and buildkitd
# trust ca.crt from the zot-tls Secret; to use a CA you already
# distribute, point zot-tls at your own issuer instead. Ten years,
# because every node holds a copy and rotating it means redistributing.
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: zot-ca
  namespace: zot
spec:
  isCA: true
  commonName: zot-ca
  secretName: zot-ca
  duration: 87600h
  privateKey:
    algorithm: ECDSA
    size: 256
  issuerRef:
    kind: Issuer
    name: zot-selfsigned
---
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: zot-ca
  namespace: zot
spec:
  ca:
    secretName: zot-ca
---
# The key that signs push tokens. Zeabur Builder reads tls.key and signs
# a short-lived token for each push; zot checks it with tls.crt. Only
# the key matters, so a renewal keeps it (rotationPolicy: Never). zot
# reads tls.crt once at start: to rotate the key, delete the Secret
# zot-token-signer, wait for cert-manager to issue it again, and restart
# zot.
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: zot-token-signer
  namespace: zot
spec:
  commonName: zot-token-signer
  secretName: zot-token-signer
  duration: 87600h
  privateKey:
    algorithm: Ed25519
    encoding: PKCS8
    rotationPolicy: Never
  issuerRef:
    kind: Issuer
    name: zot-selfsigned
releases.name: tls

profiles.multi-node:
# Still one replica: filesystem storage has a single writer, and the
# ReadWriteOnce volume binds it to one node anyway.
replicaCount: 1
resources:
  # More concurrent pushes and pulls.
  requests: {cpu: 50m, memory: 128Mi}
  limits: {memory: 1Gi}

releases.values:
# Pinned by digest; a tag alone can move.
image:
  repository: ghcr.io/project-zot/zot
  tag: v2.1.22@sha256:96cda11459ce6f8c60da3b03f03e9f67fd11b3ae2d82c4c04c92b3c608996080
service:
  # Anyone may pull: never on node ports (the chart's
  # default is NodePort).
  type: ClusterIP
  port: 5000
  # Set by the clusterIp input; the certificate below names it.
  clusterIP: ""
httpGet:
  # The probes must speak TLS once zot does.
  scheme: HTTPS
# StatefulSet with a volumeClaimTemplate; images survive restarts.
persistence: true
pvc:
  # One size for both profiles: volumeClaimTemplates can't change, so a
  # profile switch would stop the upgrade. local-path ignores the size;
  # on Longhorn, grow the claim when about 20 builds of a few apps no
  # longer fit.
  storage: 20Gi
# The restricted Pod Security level. The image has no user of its own,
# so any UID works; fsGroup gives it the volume and the mounted Secrets.
podSecurityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true
  runAsUser: 65532
  runAsGroup: 65532
  fsGroup: 65532
  seccompProfile:
    type: RuntimeDefault
securityContext:
  # A process gains no privilege that its parent lacks.
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  capabilities:
    # zot binds port 5000 and needs no capability.
    drop: [ALL]
extraObjects:
  # The serving certificate; the pod starts once its Secret exists.
  # localhost and 127.0.0.1 let a node pull through a loopback
  # port-forward; the last address is the fixed ClusterIP, or ::1 when
  # there is none. zot reloads the certificate when cert-manager renews
  # it.
  - apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
    kind: Certificate
    metadata:
      name: zot-tls
      namespace: zot
    spec:
      secretName: zot-tls
      dnsNames:
        - zot.zot.svc
        - zot.zot.svc.cluster.local
        - localhost
      ipAddresses:
        - 127.0.0.1
        - '{{ .Values.service.clusterIP | default "::1" }}'
      privateKey:
        algorithm: ECDSA
        size: 256
      issuerRef:
        kind: Issuer
        name: zot-ca
# The chart stores config in a Secret named zot-config and mounts it at
# /etc/zot. configFiles stays empty: the chart refuses both.
configFiles:
  config.json: null
# The chart mounts config from its own Secret; no ConfigMap.
mountConfig: false
# The serving certificate. The pod waits for the Secret.
externalSecrets:
  - secretName: zot-tls
    mountPath: /tls
# Only tls.crt of zot-token-signer, to check tokens: zot never gets
# the key that signs them. The pod waits for the Secret.
extraVolumes:
  - name: token
    secret:
      secretName: zot-token-signer
      items:
        - {key: tls.crt, path: tls.crt}
# bearer.cert reads it from here.
extraVolumeMounts:
  - name: token
    mountPath: /token
    readOnly: true
config:
  # Referrers and artifactType, which source archives use.
  distSpecVersion: 1.1.1
  # No search or UI extensions: they keep an index in memory. No
  # read/write timeouts: the chart's 60s cuts off large layer pushes.
  storage:
    rootDirectory: /var/lib/registry
    dedupe: true
    gc: true
    gcDelay: 2h
    gcInterval: 1h
    # Every untagged manifest goes after the delay; per repository, the
    # 20 most recently pushed tags stay. Builder pushes one tag per
    # commit, so 20 commits remain to roll back to.
    retention:
      delay: 2h
      policies:
        - repositories: ["**"]
          deleteReferrers: true
          deleteUntagged: true
          keepTags:
            - mostRecentlyPushedCount: 20
  http:
    # All interfaces, so the Service reaches the pod.
    address: 0.0.0.0
    # The Service port.
    port: "5000"
    # The certificate and key from the zot-tls Secret.
    tls:
      cert: /tls/tls.crt
      key: /tls/tls.key
    # Pushes, deletes and source reads need a token from Zeabur Builder,
    # signed with the key of zot-token-signer. A token names each
    # repository exactly, such as team-a/api and team-a/api/source, and
    # expires. zot checks such a request against the token alone, not
    # against accessControl. realm is required, but clients send the
    # token without asking it.
    auth:
      bearer:
        realm: https://zot.zot.svc:5000/zot/auth/token
        service: zot
        cert: /token/tls.crt
    # Requests without a token. zot applies the rule with the longest
    # pattern, not the union of matches. Everyone pulls images. Nobody
    # reads source archives (<namespace>/<build>/source).
    accessControl:
      repositories:
        "**":
          anonymousPolicy: [read]
        "**/source":
          policies: []
  # Requests and errors only.
  log:
    level: info

releases.name: builder

profiles.single-node:
resources:
  # The controller only; each namespace's buildkitd sizes itself. Idles near 6Mi.
  requests: {cpu: 10m, memory: 16Mi}
  limits: {memory: 256Mi}
extraArgs:
  # Each namespace's build cache on the node's disk.
  - --buildkitd-cache-size=10Gi

releases.values:
registry:
  # zot above: images go to zot.zot.svc:5000/<namespace>/<build>.
  host: zot.zot.svc:5000
  # zot's token signer: each build pushes with a short-lived token for
  # its own repositories only.
  tokenKey:
    namespace: zot
    secret: zot-token-signer
  # buildkitd trusts zot's own CA, copied from the zot-tls Secret at
  # install time.
  caFrom:
    namespace: zot
    secret: zot-tls
  # The egress policy lets buildkitd reach zot's pods on 5000; every
  # other private address stays blocked.
  inCluster:
    namespace: zot
    podLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: zot}
    port: 5000

security.summary: Zeabur Builder: a ClusterRole that manages Builds, BuildRuns and Jobs in every namespace; reads Pods and Namespaces; reads, creates, updates and deletes Secrets in every namespace (the Git credentials Builds name, and the copies it puts in build namespaces), and reads the zot token signer. Runs one privileged buildkitd per building namespace in its own namespace, with a user namespace and an egress policy. An admission policy limits the Jobs and StatefulSets it can create. zot: no RBAC, a ServiceAccount without roles; serves the OCI registry API over TLS on port 5000 inside the cluster.

smoke.manifest:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: {name: smoke, namespace: zot}
spec:
  backoffLimit: 6
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 65532
        seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}
      containers:
        - name: curl
          image: curlimages/curl:8.23.0@sha256:3fb7e13e5d179a845c97d78204f3f1064d1907037f26a3ebf91710571151fd93
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}
          args: [-sSf, --cacert, /tls/ca.crt, "https://zot.zot.svc:5000/v2/"]
          volumeMounts: [{name: tls, mountPath: /tls}]
      volumes: [{name: tls, secret: {secretName: zot-tls}}]
smoke.name: tls-v2
